newsitem.title: UK: Final Thai sugar extraction rates seen under targe.
newsitem.headline: Final Thai sugar extraction rates seen under targe.

text.p: Sugar extraction rates in Thailand could fall short of the desired target level as mills remelt raw sugar into white to cover earlier export committments, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
This season's extraction rate was running at 10.289 percent, down on the final rate of 10.383 percent reported last year when the remelt programme had closed.
Last year at this point the extraction rate was running at some 10.548 percent before mills had completed remelting, Czarnikow said in its monthly report.

"Such reprocessing inevitably entails a further slight loss of sugar so that the overall net extraction rate from cane slips from the initial rate for raw sugar prior to the remelt programme picking up," it said.

"There may well be some further slippage by the time that the remelt programme finishes so that this year's level will be well short of the target 10.4 to 10.5 percent hoped for by the close of the five year plan."
Czarnikow said raw sugar could be converted to white at low cost in a narrow window which existed while there was sufficient bagasse to power the mills.
